$comment: Zirconium kernel configuration.
This file is the single source of truth for what the kernel contains and
what it does at boot.  `zig build` compiles it into a Zig module that the
kernel reads at compile time; nothing in the kernel hardcodes a value that
lives here.
Build-time overrides:
-Dconfig=<path>        use a different configuration file
-Dselftest=true        turn the `selftest` feature on (same as editing
features.selftest below)

timer.$comment: Tick rate of the system timer, in hertz.

heap.$comment: Size of the kernel heap, in kibibytes.

network.$comment: Static addressing used until (and unless) DHCP replaces it.

$comment: Compile-time feature switches.  A feature that is off removes its code
from the kernel entirely, and any boot stage that requires it is
dropped from the boot sequence.
The boot sequence, in order.
A stage may name a feature in `requires`.  If that feature is off, the
stage is dropped from the sequence, so turning `network` off removes the
network stage without having to edit this list as well.
The machines this ZVM runs.  This is the heart of the configuration: a
virtual machine monitor is defined by the machines it runs, not by the
host's own features.
name      - the name the operator sees
profile   - the machine the guest is shown; 'auto' lets the
hypervisor decide from what the guest turns out to need
image     - the guest's kernel image, on the host's filesystem
autostart - whether the machine is started at boot
cores     - vCPUs to give it; 0 lets the partitioner decide
ram_mb    - RAM to give it; 0 lets the partitioner decide
order     - the order the machines are started in
